chains.name: Unauthenticated XXE → Remote Code Execution
chains.vulnerabilities: XXE, Missing Security Header (CSP, X‑XXP), Missing Rate Limiting
chains.impact: Full server compromise – an attacker can read sensitive files (e.g., `/etc/passwd`, application configs) and eventually execute arbitrary code by leveraging the XXE parser to include external entities.

chains.name: SQL Injection + Missing Rate Limiting → Database Domination
chains.vulnerabilities: SQLi, Missing Rate Limiting, Missing Security Header (CSP)
chains.impact: Complete database takeover – unlimited login attempts allow credential stuffing to obtain valid sessions, while the SQLi in `post_body` enables extraction, modification, or deletion of all data, potentially leading to admin account creation.

chains.name: Mass Assignment → Privilege Escalation + Open‑Redirect Phishing → Account Takeover
chains.vulnerabilities: Mass Assignment (auto_dispatch), Open Redirect (to), XSS (auto_dispatch), Missing Security Header (CSP, RP)
chains.impact: Attacker first uses the mass‑assignment flaw to set `isAdmin:true` or similar fields on `/api/users/me`. The open‑redirect (`/redirect?to=`) is then abused to send the victim to a malicious site that hosts an XSS payload (leveraging the weak CSP). The XSS steals the victim’s session cookie, which, combined with the escalated privileges, yields full account takeover.

chains.name: Missing Rate Limiting + Credential Stuffing → Unauthenticated Account Takeover
chains.vulnerabilities: Missing Rate Limiting, Unknown (post_body, to), Missing Security Header (HSTS, PP)
chains.impact: Because the login endpoint imposes no throttling, an attacker can automate credential‑stuffing against the `/login` endpoint (or any endpoint that accepts authentication tokens). Successful logins give direct access to user accounts, especially when missing HSTS/PP allow session hijacking via MITM or cookie theft.
